slides.title: Pelican Packaging: reserve, build or bridge?

paragraphs.text: Pelican Packaging: reserve, build or bridge?
Recommendation on the second molding-line installation slot, the full line order and temporary overflow capacity · Investment Committee pre-read for decision at the January 2027 IC
Pelican Packaging
Investment committee
Synthetic benchmark data · built only from the IC briefing pack; no external research · cash figures exclude 2027–30 operating cash flow, which the pack does not give

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Reserve the slot as a capped $0.6M option, bridge 2028 with the contract molder, and order the line only once signed demand and funding clear set triggers
The gap is real and starts in 2028, but its size hinges on unsigned demand
–	On accepted units the line is 92% used in 2027, not 83%; overflow starts in 2028 (0.6M)
–	Overflow hits 3.5M units by 2030 at forecast, 0.9M at signed minimums; 2.6M is unsigned
–	The 98% fill rate is monthly; two misses let a customer rebid its whole allocation
Ordering now breaks the cash covenant; doing nothing breaks the fill-rate standard
–	A full order leaves $4.0M of cash, $3.0M under the $7.0M floor, with no facility
–	Doing nothing leaves 0.6M units unserved in 2028, 3.5M by 2030; the molder is 1.0M short in 2030
The slot is a capped option worth buying, provided the order date can move
–	Cash stays $1.2M above the floor, at most $0.6M is lost, and it pays only by protecting allocations
–	It expects a June 2027 order, but funding is only plausible in 2028: agree a later date first
Three hard triggers turn the reservation into a full order
–	Demand: 10.5M+ units signed for 2029 or 2030 (now 9.4M / 9.8M), or a simulated 2-month breach
–	Funding: $3.5M+ committed, so cash after the $4.2M payment stays at $7.5M or more
–	Readiness: supplier dates and validation plan confirmed; decide Q1 2028, Q3 at the latest

paragraphs.text: One bad month can cost an allocation
▪	Standard: a 98% fill rate every month for every customer; two misses give the right to rebid the whole allocation, not just the units missed
▪	Peaks: several launches in one six-week window can exceed the monthly rate even when the year fits (plant supervisor); molder holiday capacity is uncommitted
▪	At stake: about $4.0M a year of base contribution (9.0M units × $0.45) is exposed; losing a quarter of it costs ~$1.0M a year, more than the $0.45M lost on the 2030 shortfall
▪	To confirm: a monthly simulation or an inventory buffer
In 2029 even the molder leaves ~2% headroom: a launch cluster could cause the two misses that open a rebid
1  Monthly rates = annual capacity ÷ 12 (even-flow simplification)
2  Contribution proxy uses the pack's $0.45 a unit for serving rather than refusing demand; the 25% loss share is an illustrative analysis assumption
Sources: IC briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis

slides.title: Cover 2028 in three layers: the contract molder booked by June 2027, a 2027 safety stock, and specialty kept in-house

paragraphs.text: 1 The need    2 The options    3 The slot decision    4 The plan and gates
Cover 2028 in three layers: the contract molder booked by June 2027, a 2027 safety stock, and specialty kept in-house
A. External capacity: book the contract molder
B. Internal buffer: build a 2027 safety stock
C. Internal mix: protect what only we can make
▪	Needed: only a January 2027 order, which breaches the covenant, beats the 2028 peak
▪	Notice is 5 months; sign by end-June 2027 to lock in holiday capacity
▪	Hold an option on up to 2.3M units for 2029 (~$0.27M)
▪	Quote specialty first-article validation as a hedge
▪	Slack of 9.0M − 8.3M exceeds the 0.6M 2028 overflow
▪	Pre-build standard containers ahead of the 2028 peak to absorb launch clustering
▪	Depends on shelf-life and customer lot rules
▪	Cap working capital so cash headroom holds (unit cost not in pack)
▪	Schedule specialty first on our own line; the molder is not validated for it
▪	Add the 4% specialty scrap allowance to the plan
▪	Run a monthly fill-rate simulation (launches, holidays, scrap) by Q2 2027
M units for 2028: 24% of ceiling, ~$0.07M
M units of 2027 practical slack
M units a year of scrap allowance
Together: up to 3.2M units of 2028 cover, ~5 times the overflow, with no fixed capex
1  The pack says the 2028 peak starts before mid-2028; the analysis assumes around Q2 2028, so the latest molder notice is about November 2027

slides.title: Release the $4.2M balance only when all three triggers are met on demand, funding and readiness

paragraphs.text: 1 The need    2 The options    3 The slot decision    4 The plan and gates
Release the $4.2M balance only when all three triggers are met on demand, funding and readiness
Demand: signed 2029 or 2030 minimums of 10.5M units or more
Funding: at least $3.5M committed, so cash after the payment is $7.5M or more
Readiness: supplier and validation plan confirmed
▪	Counts take-or-pay or prepaid volume
▪	OR: simulation shows 2+ months below 98% with the molder at contracted capacity
▪	Why 10.5M: signed overflow (~1.6M) uses two-thirds of the ceiling; under half of the other 1.9M forecast units would exhaust it
▪	$8.2M − $4.2M + $3.5M = $7.5M: the $7.0M floor plus a $0.5M buffer
▪	Customer prepayment, or a loan backed by a signed-volume guarantee; pricing to negotiate
▪	One signed-volume guarantee can meet two triggers: it adds demand and secures the loan
▪	Plan allows +2 months for specialty validation
▪	Molder bridge contracted through commissioning
▪	Construction inflation re-quoted
M units signed (today 9.4M / 9.8M)
balance due after the credited deposit
months to install, fixed price, confirmed
Not triggers: 'demand is growing', nonbinding forecasts, peer growth statistics, or a wish to announce capacity publicly
1  The 10.5M threshold and the $0.5M buffer are the analysis's proposals (policy choices, not in the pack; unverified)
2  Internal capacity after specialty scrap ~8.9M + molder 2.5M = ~11.4M of demand coverable without the line
Sources: Analysis deck: proposals and assumptions not in the pack (unverified); IC briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis
